title: Xdrip stops receiving data from G6 after Bluetooth failed to register error and requires reboot.
body:
### Subject of the issue
The latest nightly (and the previous few) stop receiving data from my Dexcom G6 after 6-24 hours and the G5/G6 Status Bluetooth Link: shows "Failed to register application for bluetooth scan" in red.

### Your environment
- What version of xDrip.
c6c289d-2021.01.03 
- What type of hardware data source and how do you get your data there
Dexcom G6 8Mxxxxx transmitter
- Is your issue specific to a device like and Android phone or a smartwatch?
Google Pixel 4A running Android 11 December 5 and now January 5 security patch
- All settings related to the issue, e.g. activated auto calibration.
G5/G6 Debug Settings (all others not listed are disabled)
[x] Use the OB1 Collector
[x] Native Algorithm
[x] Minimize Scanning
[x] G6 Support
[x] Allow OB1 unbonding
[x] Allow OB1 to initiate bonding
Bluetooth Settings (all others not listed are disabled)
[x] Turn Bluetooth on
[x] Bluetooth Watchdog
[x] G5 Bluetooth Watchdog
[x] Trust Auto-Connect
[x] Use Background Scans
[x] Allow blucon unbonding

### Expected behavior
XDrip should keep receiving data from G6 device.

### Actual behavior
XDrip fails to receive data from G6 device after 6-24 hours with the "Failed to register application for bluetooth scan" and requires a phone reboot to begin receiving data again.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Let XDrip run.
It seems like going out of range, so that a reading is missed can trigger it sometimes, but not always.  Also, pairing bluetooth headphones or a heart-rate monitor can also trigger it sometimes.  Seems like anything that changes bluetooth on the phone in some way can be the trigger.

NOTE: I uploaded LOGs showing this happening over multiple reboots.

So, I realized this happened because my Garmin 645 watch vibrates when it loses Bluetooth connection.  While XDrip was showing the error, my Garmin Connect software was also unable to talk to my watch.  I manually turned off Bluetooth and turned it back on.  After a little while, the Garmin reconnected, but XDrip was still still showing the error.  I manually force-stopped XDrip and then restarted the collector and it eventually started working again.

Looking through the logs it's been dorked since 1 AM last night and has been attempting to stop/re-start bluetooth a whole bunch of times since then.  It basically got no data from 1-9 AM (then backfilled to 6 AM), which happens to coincide with when I was sleeping.  I wonder if this is a phone deep-sleeping problem?  I have XDrip set to not-optimized, but it's rather a strange coincidence that it all started when I set the phone down and went to sleep and was able to get things working again when I woke up and picked up the phone.  The death at 10AM also coincides with the phone having been set down for a while.

Do you have the option "Close GATT on BLE disconnect" checked or not? I suggest having it checked.

When you get the message saying `failure to register` and need to reboot the phone I am pretty sure this happens when the actual Bluetooth stack in the android operating system fails. This is why you need to reboot to fix it and toggling Bluetooth off/on isn't sufficient to reset it. I have seen this before on Android 7-8.1 of various platforms but particularly with broadcom chipsets and definitely traced it to the stack itself, but I thought it was fixed in Android 9+ so if the Pixel 4a is up to date then I'm surprised to hear of that issue being reported there.

There are two known existing bugs that hasn't been adressed, there is a PR for them which fixes both. One is there is a new format for one of the info messages, the other that there is a mismatch in the current understanding of what the characteristics services offer which means there are attempts to READ instead of INDICATE in three places. That this causes intermittent problems and issues that manifest in different ways depends on
1: your Android version
2: the vendor of the BT software stack and in most cases hardware
3: Possibly some other unknown factor like phone vendor modifications in the layer between application and hardware.

Considering this was first reported in March last year and the PR has existed since November I can only hope that someone notices.
